definition: Source-by-source audit of six supplied scans. “Printed vocabulary” covers explicit word labels, word banks, the title and the lesson’s named grammar forms. “Additional vocabulary” covers useful content words in instructions, choices, examples and readings. “Useful expressions” covers source-printed collocations and language frames. Each glossary entry is unique within the lesson, belongs to one category, includes an Arabic meaning and a source excerpt, and lists every source image where it appears. Character names, isolated numerals, ordinary function words, sound/letter symbols and uncompleted dotted gaps are excluded unless they are lesson targets; all meaningful content words from the reading and activity choices are included.

reconciliation.uniqueEntries: Every glossary id and normalized English term occurs once, belongs to exactly one category, and has one Arabic meaning.
reconciliation.sourceCoverage: Each entry sourceImages list is mirrored exactly in that category’s per-image id lists; source page and SHA-256 are included per image.
reconciliation.imageOccurrences: Per-image counts sum to occurrences.allReferences; entries appearing on multiple scans contribute one reference on each scan.
reconciliation.semanticReview: All six source scans were visually reviewed on 2026-11-14. Every entry and image allocation was checked against the page; the Workbook p.16 reading terms like, one and other were verified, and the picture-only car reference on Pupil’s Book p.12 was removed.

review.method: Visually compared all six byte-preserved source scans with their page transcriptions; checked every vocabulary term, excerpt and source-image allocation against the corresponding scan; corrected unsupported picture-only or page references; reconciled category and occurrence totals.
review.translationNote: Arabic meanings are editorial learner-support glosses; they are not claimed to be printed textbook translations.
review.scopeNote: Picture-only labels, character names, ordinary function words, isolated numerals, and uncompleted dotted gaps remain excluded under the audit definition. The Workbook reading additions like, one, and other are included because they carry meaning in the printed passage.
